A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mallows-DPO work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original proofs, experimental details, and qualitative comparisons can be matched across appendix and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original bandit simulations, IMDB generation experiments, and Pythia-2.8B preference evaluations on Anthropic HH and out-of-distribution datasets, with qualitative examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds a synthetic dispersion-estimator check and Llama3-8B-Instruct experiments using UltraFeedback and Alpaca Eval V2.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the Mallows-θ/ϕ objectives, entropy-based dispersion proxy, and sigmoid/polynomial approximations. Clarified notation and the corrected estimator restatement in Section 5.1 do not establish a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Section 5.5 adds preference training on UltraFeedback prompts with generated, reward-ranked responses and response-quality evaluation on Alpaca Eval V2. This substantially extends the empirical data coverage beyond the retained bandit, IMDB, Anthropic HH, SHP, and H4 Stack Exchange experiments.

E2.justification: BT-DPO remains the evaluated external comparator in the retained experiments and the new Llama3 comparison. SimPO, ORPO, and other newly discussed methods are not added as evaluated baselines; ArmoRM supplies preference rankings rather than serving as a competing optimization method.

E3.justification: The new Llama3-8B-Instruct experiment generates five responses per UltraFeedback prompt, selects the best/worst using ArmoRM, compares three β values at two learning rates, and reports LC and ordinary win rates on Alpaca Eval V2. Section 3.3 also introduces a ranking-sampling protocol for estimator validation. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 directly tests the entropy proxy against known synthetic dispersion in Section 3.3/Figure 1, examines high/low dispersion prompts in Figure 6 and new Appendix A, and tests the Llama3 comparison across β and learning-rate choices. These substantially expand diagnostics; the original robustness results and twelve response-comparison tables remain.

E5.justification: Section 5.5 newly reports ten generation seeds at the selected Llama3 setting, with means, ± values, and error bars in Figure 11. This adds uncertainty reporting for one experiment, but does not establish repeated training runs. The uncertainty statistic is not explicitly defined, and no formal significance test is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds synthetic estimator-alignment findings and Alpaca Eval V2 results. Table 2 reports Mallows/DPO LC win rates of 43.10%/42.55% at β=0.01 and learning rate 5e-7, but 39.75%/40.56% at β=0.05 with that learning rate. Figure 11 adds generation-seed summaries. These are new results; the original performance figures and qualitative comparison tables are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 changes the Ψ assumption from decreasing to non-decreasing. Theorem 2 replaces the fixed e in Equation 22 with t=ϕ(x), and Section 3.2 expands the stated dispersion domain to include 1. These are local formal revisions; the theorem structure and appendix proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit first-work claim for mathematically grounded ranking-based pairwise preference optimization beyond Bradley–Terry, and claims estimator validation and statistically supported improvement. The conclusion explicitly extends effectiveness to Llama3-8B-Instruct. The central dispersion-aware optimization and unification contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains how high-dispersion pairs receive less weight and low-dispersion pairs more weight, and interprets the normalized negative-log estimate relative to the dataset. Future work broadens from alternative regularizers to combining Mallows with other DPO variants. The existing unresolved questions about mechanism and β selection remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies N=max(|Yw|,|Yl|) for the entropy approximation and documents the new Llama3 response-ranking recipe and hyperparameter grid. The original optimizer, batch-size, warmup, bandit-training, and GPT-4 judging details are retained in the renumbered experimental appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for ODPO, ORPO, SimPO, RLHFlow, Llama 3, and ArmoRM, and expands discussion of reference-free methods and f-DPO. It also makes the beyond-Bradley–Terry novelty claim explicit. This updates positioning while retaining the original literature foundation.

P1.justification: The contribution paragraph becomes four numbered items, ranking-model and dispersion explanations are expanded, and terminology distinguishes dispersion from negative-log dispersion. A new experimental subsection and appendix are inserted, but the six-section main structure and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds estimator-validation, prompt-example, and generation-seed figures (Figures 1, 6, and 11), a hyperparameter-results table, and two prompt-example tables. It also redraws the dispersion histograms with clearer axis labels and common horizontal ranges. Existing plots and appendix comparisons are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The controlled estimator check and Llama3 comparison with matched hyperparameter choices provide useful additional support for the dispersion proxy and broader applicability. Clearer interpretation and the corrected Ψ monotonicity assumption also improve the paper. The gains remain limited: estimator validation is synthetic, uncertainty covers generation seeds only, and the new statistical-significance claim is not supported by a reported formal test.
